In this study, to accelerate the computation of indices, a different hybrid contingency reduction method is also introduced. The effectiveness of the proposed algorithm is tested on a 24-bus IEEE reliability test system.

articleTitle: TCSC control based on linear matrix inequality
abstract: In this paper TCSC controller is designed based on linear matrix inequality (LMI) control theory for a multimachine system. Anderson's 3-machine 9-bus system model is used to discuss the robustness of the proposed method, in which the load is power-constant model. LMI-based H/sub /spl infin// control theory is successfully used to design a TCSC controller to improve robustness, which can realize adjustment of control speed by adding pole placement constraint, neglecting weighting matrix. The pole region placement based on system's dominant poles may be applied to various visual control designs. The load model in this paper is simple and some difference would be found against actual load.

articleTitle: Frequency domain analysis of 110/35 kV transformer station grounding system subject to lightning strike
abstract: Lightning transients processes appear when lightning strikes hit tall objects, such as transmission and communication towers or transformer substations. Large currents generated by the stroke flow in the grounding system and dissipate in the soil. The electromagnetic fields (EMF) generated by such high currents may cause damage to equipment and may be dangerous to personnel. The field theory method is used to examine the transient behaviour of the lightning processes in the grounding system.

articleTitle: Allocation of fixed transmission costs among generators: a what-if analysis based method
abstract: This paper proposes an economic indicator we called assistance ratio which could be used to assess the part of fixed transmission costs to be allocated to "assistance", or short-term, users as opposed to "normal", or long-term, users in a transmission pricing system based on a postage stamp method. Short-term users are mostly consumers having their own generating plants, so they produce flows on the network only when their facilities are out of order. The indicator is calculated as the ratio of the cost of the virtual network which would be needed to convey assistance flows if all generating facilities were located close to the loads and the cost of the actual network. A case study is carried out on the 24-bus IEEE Reliability Test System.

articleTitle: Dynamic identification and control of PWM inverter VAr compensator using neural network
abstract: The performance and dynamic characteristic of a solid-state VAr compensator controlled by a neural network is presented and analyzed. Neural network based indirect model reference adaptive control (NN-MRAC) theory is used to design the multioutput nonlinear controller structure. Simulation results of the closed loop control system using a multioutput nonlinear neural network controller demonstrate desirable reactive power compensation and voltage regulation.

articleTitle: Two various control laws for controllable series capacitor (CSC)
abstract: A controllable series capacitor (CSC) with suitable control schemes can improve power system transient stability and help to damp electromechanical oscillations. This paper examines the improvement of power system dynamics when a CSC is controlled by either a control Lyapunov function (CLF) or variable structure control (VSC). The effectiveness of the proposed control laws are demonstrated in a single machine infinite bus (SMIB) power system.

articleTitle: Symbolic analysis aid to power flows graphing in open electricity market
abstract: The costing and pricing of electricity is the key issue of the liberalization process. The power and the energy produced, consumed and exchanged between the two parties, i.e. the trading products, are traditionally monitored by the AC or the DC load flow solutions and/or participation factors. The paper proposes the symbolic analysis of the DC load flow solution and the computer program SADCLF (the symbolic simulator) as an aid to the problem of the power flows graphing (visualization). Transactions are allocated and their net impact on transmission are easily visualized using the proposed method.

articleTitle: Methodological and practical aspects of steady-state security assessment of Yugoslav Power System
abstract: The relevant methodological and practical aspects of steady-state security assessment of Yugoslav Power System are presented in this paper. This methodology consists of a procedure for forming the unified external network equivalents, procedure for fast contingency selection and simple method for the fast assessment of dynamic change of power system frequency. Full contingency analysis is based on a specially developed method, which enables successive solution of the load-flow problem for a set of characteristic post-dynamic quasi-stationary states. The characteristics of the developed methodology are tested on the example of the existing electric power interconnection in the Balkans.

articleTitle: A travelling wave technique for assessing the transient response of grounding electrodes
abstract: Transient behavior of grounding electrodes cannot be accurately determined using existing modeling techniques, as these are normally applied to grounding resistance calculation under a 50 Hz excitation. In this paper, a new technique is proposed to model the transient behavior of power system grounding electrodes based on the calculation of travelling waves. Results are compared to those obtained by applying the established technique published and they are of a comparable form to those from literature.

articleTitle: Transmission line EMF mitigation: managing the uncertainty
abstract: Transmission and distribution utilities are still investigating ways in which they can reduce public fear of adverse health effects from exposure to magnetic fields. Responding to utilities' need in this area, a comprehensive effort has been initiated to provide utilities with the tool they need to develop their own strategies for meeting EMF abatement goals in the most cost-effective manner. In order to define how well potential solutions can satisfy utility problems, a list of prioritized criteria used in utility decision making was developed. The criteria were grouped into four major categories: technical performance; cost; environmental issues; and risks. A multi-attribute analysis can help policy makers identify least-cost mitigation strategies from a global perspective.

articleTitle: An incomplete acceleration constant method improving convergency for transient load flow calculation
abstract: This paper presents an efficient transient load flow calculation using an incomplete acceleration method. This method does not use the LU factorization, which is the most time consuming part of a load flow calculation. Therefore, fast calculation can be carried out. The proposed method can be applied for the methods that have more inferior convergency than the Newton-Raphson method. To confirm the effectiveness of the proposed method, test calculations were carried out. The results show that the proposed, method is able to improve convergency remarkably than the constant Jacobian method and is faster than the Newton-Raphson method.

articleTitle: Some considerations concerning the choice of material and design for composite insulators to be used in Public Enterprise of Bosnia Herzegovina transmission lines
abstract: This paper describes the approach being used in Public Enterprise Elektroprivreda of Bosnia Herzegovina (EP BiH) for future selection of material and design for composite insulators (CI) to be used in its transmission lines. This approach is based on learning from the experiences belonging to someone else, as well as on the authors' own experience gained by practical use and monitoring of the composite insulators installed. The results of the research work undertaken during several past years is a preliminary in-house technical specification which is to be a document of "dynamic nature"-being changed (improved) according to all approved technical knowledge gathered by other utilities on all over the world.

articleTitle: LQG decentralized controls for FACTS based on structure of modeling by subsystems
abstract: It is well known that the main disadvantage of centralized controls systems in power systems is the time delay that is produced by communication systems. This paper presents a design technique of decentralized LQG controllers, which conserves the optimality characteristic of an LQR regulator. The design of these controllers is based on a proposed structure of subsystems of low order, which can be calculated using either order reduction techniques or identification techniques. This structure is noncoupled in state variables, that allows the computation of independent LQR regulators. The paper presents the calculation of equivalent estimators for each subsystem taking into account the other optimal controllers. The proposed method is used to coordinate two SVC controllers. Results of simulations of the controlled system are shown.

articleTitle: Software package for short-term planning of the Croatian power system
abstract: This paper presents software for the short-term operative planning of the Croatian power system, based on the simulation principle, including some optimization modules. The software is designed in such a way that it enables a simple and quick making of different variants of the daily power system schedule. It also enables an improvement on all functions as well as the superstructure and redesigning, which will make possible the undisturbed functioning of the operative planning in the Croatian power system during the process of restructuring, deregulation and privatization.

articleTitle: On optimal space distribution of ready-reserve in a power system-comprehensive approach
abstract: This article presents an emergency control system, the results of a series of the offline procedures, designed to act correctively in the case of transmission line outages. The corrective actions have to do with introducing various forms of active and reactive operating reserves (spinning reserve, ready reserve, VAr equipment and load shedding). The suggested methodology, applied through the mentioned procedures, results in information arrangeable in tables and/or a chart of introducing particular segments of the operating reserve, together with the already scheduled generators, selecting the one suited best for the actual level and distribution of the system's load.

articleTitle: Behavior of an induction motor supplied from a voltage controlled current regulated PWM inverter
abstract: In this paper an overview of the behavior of an induction motor when it is supplied from a voltage controlled current regulated inverter is presented. The objective is to show that in this condition, the motor behaves very closely to when it is supplied from the mains. In addition, it is emphasized that unlike the other types of inverters-voltage source or current source, PWM inverters-voltage and current waveforms at motor terminals are nearly sinusoidal and the harmonic content of voltage and current is very low. In this paper, only one type of current regulator is discussed (free running hysteresis current regulator) but other types of regulator such as fixed frequency hysteresis regulator could be used in the system. The simulation result depicts the start-up and loading characteristic of the motor. These results could be compared to those of an induction motor fed from mains supply.

articleTitle: Insulation breakdown of field winding in turbine-generator fed from static exciter
abstract: The paper is concerned with the additional voltage stress in the field winding of turbine-generator produced by a thyristor exciter. In few cases, the insulation of field winding was damaged within a short time (some months) after commissioning the static exciters, although previously these rotors were in service with a DC rotating exciter without any trouble for many years. The current paper describes the experimental results of the study searching for a possible reason for the failure.

articleTitle: Probabilistic assessment of the sag in an overhead transmission line
abstract: The sag in an overhead transmission line is significantly influenced by the current in the line conductor. Using the deterministic method to determine current carrying capacity of a conductor is too conservative. In recent times however, some power utility companies are using the real-time monitoring approach. This is very costly and cannot be adopted by all. A new method, based on probabilistic techniques, is used to assess the sag in an overhead line in this paper.

articleTitle: Breakdown characteristics of CO/sub 2/ and N/sub 2/ containing SF/sub 6/ at different gap spacings
abstract: AC breakdown strengths of CO/sub 2/, N/sub 2/, SF/sub 6/ and the mixtures of CO/sub 2/+SF/sub 6/ and N/sub 2/+SF/sub 6/ containing 0.5% and 4% of SF/sub 6/ in a nonuniform field were experimentally studied. The relative gas pressure and the electrode gap spacing were varied within the range of 100-500 kPa and of 5-20 mm respectively. The experimental results have shown that the addition of SF/sub 6/ to CO/sub 2/ and N/sub 2/ causes a significant increase the AC breakdown voltage with respect to CO/sub 2/ and N/sub 2/.

articleTitle: Automatic fault location using intelligent processing
abstract: This paper describes an automatic fault location technique for permanent faults in underground low voltage distribution networks (ULVDNs). It uses signals from an existing time domain reflectometry (TDR) instrument. It preprocesses TDR signals to eliminate single phase problem, and to locate 3-phase open or short circuit faults and also uses adaptive filtering to produce enhanced difference between the TDR signal to locate faults. The relative performance of the system is demonstrated using field data.

articleTitle: Probabilistic assessment of the sag in an overhead transmission line
abstract: The sag in an overhead transmission line is significantly influenced by the current in the line conductor. Using the deterministic method to determine the current carrying capacity of a conductor is too conservative. In recent times, however, some power utility companies have used a real-time monitoring approach. This is very costly and cannot be adopted by all. A new method, based on probabilistic techniques, is used to assess the sag in an overhead power line in this paper. Recorded data on some climatic factors and transmission line current are used in the authors' analyses.

articleTitle: Performance tests of barriers and power line conductor guards
abstract: Tests were conducted in order to measure the 60 Hz AC breakdown voltage of small air gaps (up to 0.2 m) formed by an energized and a grounded electrode. In Phases 1 and 2 energized rod-grounded rod, and energized conductor-grounded rod gaps were studied with a flat insulating sheet (barrier) between the electrodes. In Phase 3 the energized electrode was a section of a power line conductor, the grounded electrode was either a rod or sphere, and the insulating cylinder (a 69 kV line guard) was on the conductor. The test results contribute to the understanding and evaluation of tools used for live-line work and the safety conditions associated with them.

articleTitle: Calculation of circuit breaker transient recovery voltages
abstract: This paper investigates the calculation of circuit breaker transient recovery voltages for the Vietnam 500 kV power system. Several events that can produce high transient recovery voltage levels on the 500 kV line breakers are studied, such as three-phase-to-ground, phase-to-phase grounded, phase-to-phase ungrounded and phase-to-ground fault clearing. The series capacitors protected by varistors, used on the Vietnam 500 kV system, play an important role to increase the TRVs across line circuit breakers when clearing fault currents. The influence of fault location on TRV is investigated. Several measures in order to reduce the TRVs are examined.

articleTitle: Adequacy of a sub-transmission system using health analysis
abstract: The conventional reliability indices of a subtransmission system are generally based on probabilistic methods and include basic load point indices and system performance indices. In spite of the fact that these probabilistic indices are well established and their evaluation techniques are well developed, many power utilities are continuing to use deterministic methods to assess the reliabilities of their systems. The reluctance by a power system planner to accept probabilistic methods in their present form dictates a need to create a bridge between the deterministic methods and the existing probabilistic techniques. This can be achieved by using a well-being framework which links the existing deterministic criteria with a probabilistic method. This paper illustrates an extension of the conventional probabilistic approach utilized in the subtransmission system in the form of health and margin indices that provide system planners with measures of system well-being in addition to more conventional risk indices.

articleTitle: Extension of the standard SCADA functionality with AI tools
abstract: The efficient control of power systems requires the up-to-date industrial supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA) standards and the latest artificial intelligence (AI) functions as well. The paper introduces the automatic event- and alarm recogniser and switching sequence generator functions and their embedding procedures into an existing SCADA system.

articleTitle: Dissipativity-based control for STATCOM
abstract: This paper describes a dissipativity-based approach for the dynamic control of FACTS devices based on voltage source inverters (VSI), such as STATCOM and UPFC. The main goal of the approach is to achieve the AC current and DC voltage regulation by shaping the energy of the closed-loop system, similarly to Lyapunov techniques. The proposed nonlinear control results in globally stable behaviour and it allows a reduction of DC capacitor storage capability, since the bandwidth of DC voltage regulation can be made comparable to that of AC currents without requiring the conventional decoupling between the DC-link voltage and AC current loops. Finally, an adaptive procedure is presented, which allows estimation of constant-but unknown-parameters and precise reference tracking. Simulation results, obtained using an ATP model of 24-pulse NPC inverters, indicate effectiveness and validity of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Corrosion detector for assessing the remaining life of old steel reinforced aluminium conductors
abstract: The durability of steel reinforced aluminium (ACSR) overhead line conductors is limited mostly by the corrosion of the steel core. A corrosion detector has been developed, operating on the nondestructive principle of measurement, to assess the degradation of the zinc galvanisation and to detect the corrosion of the steel core. After many laboratory measurements, the instrument was developed further for field usage on switched-off overhead lines. The corrosion detector is a mobile data logger, which can be rolled along the conductor. By the analysis of a measured voltage vector, different stages of the corrosion process can be detected.

articleTitle: How to check the reliability of a model in power systems?
abstract: The concept of structural stability (SS) is introduced. A single machine infinite bus power system is analysed from the perspective of SS. Linear, nonlinear and time-dependent perturbations are applied to the system. The full phase space of the SMIB is represented and the SS is evaluated. The model is extended by introducing a load and the influence of the load model is studied. It is shown that the SS of a model provides some valuable information about the reliability of that model.

articleTitle: Some problems of the active power enhancement of the high power arc furnaces
abstract: An often-used method for intensification of the high power arc furnaces is to increase the length of the arc. In this case it is usually necessary to change the furnace transformer and the electrode controller. Of course, due to the higher power, the conditions of the connection to the supply network are also investigated. The paper gives the analyses of the experiences gained at such an intensification process primarily focusing on the low frequency EMC problems. Measurement results are shown to illustrate the observed phenomena.

articleTitle: Reliability calculation of power transits
abstract: The paper presents an approach to model power transits in reliability calculations with special regard to the evaluation of the reliability of power transits and the effects of transits on other system customers. The attributes of the transit model as well as the model of reserve power injections are described in detail. Furthermore the paper presents a reliability calculation regarding a realistic power system. The reliability parameters of special customers are compared for calculations of today's state without power transits and for a possible future transit scenario to show the impact of power transits on system reliability. Furthermore the reliability parameters of the power transits are defined and calculated to determine how reliable a transit can be guaranteed.

articleTitle: A statistical study for switching over-voltages and risk of failure evaluation in Kuwait EHV network
abstract: In this paper, a statistical study of the switching overvoltages (SOVs) of Kuwait EHV (275 kV) is presented. The statistical simulations include different types of faults (L-G, LL-G, 3L-G, L-L), line energization and successful line reclosure. The EMTP program is used to simulate the network for this study. The probability distributions for both system overvoltages and insulation breakdown are deduced. The objective is to determine the risk of system insulation failure at the critical spots of the system, and accordingly, to assess the system insulators which are currently in use. Surge arresters are introduced in the network in order to assess their effect in reducing the risk of failure of the insulation.

articleTitle: Using sensitivity coefficients for power swing protection
abstract: Tripping of a transmission line during a power swing causes instability of a power system. When a power swing occurs, distance relays are tripped. In such a case it is necessary to set the power swing blocking relay such that unwanted operation does not occur. To achieve that, first power swing should be analyzed. Second, probability of fault occurrence must be found. Finally, settings of power swing relays must be calculated.

articleTitle: Framework for allocation of loss and security driven network capital costs in distribution systems
abstract: This paper presents a framework for development of time-of-use location-specific network use-of-system charges for distribution systems. The proposed framework is based on the concept of the reference network and treats the pricing problem as a two-stage process involving network design in the first instance followed by allocation of the resultant network capital costs amongst the users of the network. Network design is itself a two-stage process, beginning with determining the capacity for pure transport of electricity followed by the extra capacity required to satisfy quality of supply requirements. A conceptual framework is presented for determining both these capacities and their allocation in which emphasis is placed on the customer rather than the utility as the driver of network investment and performance.

articleTitle: Higher order dynamic load models in small-signal stability studies
abstract: The paper presents some of the results obtained in the study of the influence of higher order load models and their parameters on the power system small-signal stability. The results of the influence of various nonlinear dynamic loads on power system small-signal stability are presented and discussed. This study is an extension of the previous studies where only first order models have been used. As the subject of this research was small signal stability of the power system, linearised models of the power system and its elements were used. Load models were incorporated in a modified Heffron-Phillips model of a synchronous machine. The power system consisting of a synchronous machine, local load, transmission line and an infinite bus was used for the analysis.

articleTitle: Fuzzy goal programming applied to the optimal reactive power flow problem
abstract: This paper integrates artificial intelligence techniques with sensitivity analysis for the formulation and resolution of the optimal reactive power flow (ORPF) problem. The objectives and constraints are transformed into fuzzy sets and the problem is solved by a fuzzy goal programming algorithm. The algorithm allows for the satisfaction of multi-objectives and constraints through the definition of a decision fuzzy function.

articleTitle: Fault effects on double three-phase-six-phase converted transmission system operation
abstract: This study covers the fault effects on double three-phase-six-phase converted systems considering sectionalized compensation schemes for the transmission lines. Compensation schemes can be appropriate solution to increase power transfer capability, improve system stability, improve voltage regulation and reactive power balance, optimise load sharing between parallel lines and reduce system losses. Six-phases can be an appropriate solution to transmit larger amounts of power in less physical space with fewer aesthetic and electrical impacts on the environment. Detailed investigations have been carried out to obtain the fault effects considering both conversion and compensation-sectionalization technologies necessary for the design of the protection schemes.

articleTitle: Setting optimisation of the automatic for prevention of the asynchronous operation in power systems
abstract: The paper considers an algorithm for automatic devices functioning meant for prevention and elimination of asynchronous operation and its instrumentation as well as selection methods for setting parameters. In the Baltic countries, microprocessor devices based on the idea of checking the angle between two simulated voltages are widely recognised. This can be explained by the arrangement of the generating equipment and by the structure of power networks in this region that made it necessary to design special methods and tools for prevention and elimination of asynchronous operation.

articleTitle: Statistical estimation of representative weeks over a year [power system operation]
abstract: In this article, we present a method to determine five weeks in the year (and their corresponding coefficients), that estimate with a good accuracy the effective annual value of important parameters, and for a representative sample of investment studies. This is aimed at reducing the number of data and time needed to perform real time operations. The method is based on optimization first, and then statistical sorting. The optimization step consists in finding out optimal coefficients for each combination of five weeks selected. The final step sorts the combinations to find the best set of weeks by using statistical tools such as principal components analysis and mobile centers classification. As a result, two sets of weeks answer the requirements, and prove that the method works well.

articleTitle: Exact decoupled rectangular coordinates state estimation with fast computation of Jacobian matrix and mismatching vectors
abstract: This paper presents an efficient data structure management technique to improve the computational process of the power system state estimation (PSSE). The paper also presents a new formulation for the exact decoupled rectangular coordinates PSSE, which makes faster state estimation possible. The performances of these techniques are evaluated using several power system networks including IEEE 14 and 30-bus systems.

articleTitle: A fuzzy Petri-net expert system for power quality classification using wavelet transform
abstract: This paper proposes a fuzzy Petri-net (FPNs) expert system for classification of the power quality (PQ) problems. Based on the wavelet transform, the proposed expert system detects and localizes in time the transients of the signals due to various fault events. By calculating related indices to the PQ, the FPNs inference-module draws possible causes of the disturbances as well as its credibility values from its knowledge base. Attributed to the FPNs structure, the knowledge expression and inference process can be achieved systematically and graphically. To verify the performance of the proposed FPNs expert system, a wide variety of disturbance signals simulated by Electromagnetic Transients Program (EMTP) package were employed. The development and the effectiveness of the proposed system as well as the testing results are presented in this paper.

articleTitle: A power sensitivity model including generator damper windings for electromechanical oscillations studies
abstract: This paper describes the derivation of a power sensitivity model including generator damper windings for power systems electromechanical oscillations studies, subjected to small disturbances on operation conditions. The need of an infinite bus representation is avoided with the linearized nodal power balance approach. This permits the model to be easily extended to multimachine systems. Due to its structure-preserving characteristic, loads modeled as nonlinear functions of voltage and frequency and all control loops can be easily taken into account. First, the model is derived for a single generator connected to an infinite bus. Then, its performance is compared with the modified Heffron-Phillips model proposed by Saidy and Hughes. Finally, the results of a two area system are presented in order to show the effect of the damper windings on the tie-line flow.

articleTitle: Medium term electric load forecasting using artificial neural networks
abstract: In the paper artificial neural networks are applied to medium term electric load forecasting for the Hungarian Electric Power System. A feedforward multi-layer network with one hidden layer was applied using the error backpropagation algorithm for the estimation of the model weights. A model description and detailed prediction error analysis are presented.

articleTitle: Power quality: increasing reliability of power substations
abstract: In the context of deregulation of the electricity market, a special effort must be made to guarantee a high level of system reliability and supply quality. EDF has developed a tool called TOPASE for characterizing faults in electric power supply, particularly in terms of frequency and duration of power cuts at substations. It is designed around a knowledge base dedicated to the reliability of high-voltage substations and an associated database. In 1998, analysis of feedback from studies carried out with TOPASE determined several evolutions that are considered desirable. Specifications for all these changes were drawn up early in 1999 and will be implemented in the industrial version of the tool before the end of the year. Approximately ten studies were carried out in 1997-1998 with TOPASE for EDF. They have generally helped operators make and justify their decisions.

articleTitle: Short-circuit test on power transformers with pressure measurement
abstract: Summary form only given. The international standard IEC 60076-5 prescribes short-circuit tests to verify the dynamic ability of power transformers to withstand short-circuits. According to the standard, before and after each short-circuit shot, the short-circuit reactance of the transformer shall be measured. The value of changing the inductive reactance caused by the dynamic effect of short-circuit current can be drawn form the conclusion of the changing the geometry of the windings. Therefore, it is a very important electrical parameter of the test object in respect of the qualification of the transformer, so the standard limits the value of changing of the inductive reactance. The High-Power Laboratory of VEIKI-VNL Electric Large Laboratories Ltd. (Budapest) has been performing short-circuit tests on transformers for years such a way, that exceeding the obligatory requirements of the standard they have been measuring the transient pressure waves in the oil tank of the transformer caused by the moving of the windings during short-circuit test. In this paper, the authors introduce their measuring method, circumstances and results.

articleTitle: Evaluate future harmonic levels in central telephone exchanges. II
abstract: The increasing share of converter loads in electric power supplies has lead to a growing concern for harmonic distortion. In 1994, the Alexandria Electricity Company (Egypt) began a research program on harmonic levels at utility and customer buses. To ensure power quality for its customers, AEC sought to characterize the harmonic distortion for each type of activities. The central telephone exchange is one of them. A series of measurements were carried out at 12 central telephone exchanges to evaluate the influence of parameters such as harmonic impedances, currents and voltages.

articleTitle: The Baltic Ring Study-transmission system simulations in the Baltic Sea region
abstract: The Baltic Ring Study was performed as a European Union TEN project in the period 1996-1998. 18 power companies and electric utility organizations from 11 countries around the Baltic Sea which are members of three nonsynchronously interconnected power system organizations investigated the possibilities of creating a common electricity market in the Baltic sea Region, emphasizing the need for environmental improvements and benefits for the customer.

articleTitle: Operation in deregulated power systems with independent power producers
abstract: Summary form only given. This paper aims to propose a game theoretical negotiation method to provide rational decisions of the power exchange for purchases and sales between electric utilities and independent power producers (IPPs) as well as prices of the electrical energy under a competitive environment, in contrast to the conventional equalizing incremental cost rule.

articleTitle: European thematic network IFS-intelligent forecasting systems
abstract: Summary form only given as follows. The European thematic network IFS brings together more than 20 universities, manufactures and end-users for the particular research objective intelligent forecasting systems. The paper describes the network structure and the national subprojects. The project is funded from the European Union by the Brite EuRam program. Countries all over Europe, from Crete and Rome in the south to Dublin and Helsinki in the north, work together in this project. The network has to install the support for the knowledge transfer, including: current overview of the state of the art and the main research activities in the field of intelligent forecasting systems; installation of common working groups between universities and industry; workshops for personnel training; and project-wide demonstrations to show the advantages of intelligent forecasting systems. The active members of the project work within three task groups: energy time series; fault and state forecasting; and modelling and control strategies. The paper reports about the IFS-activities, more than 20 national subprojects and a IFS Workshop 99 in Vienna in this field especially of results on the following horizontal themes between all national subprojects: robustness and online-capability of forecasting systems; exactness and validity of the prediction; data preparing for predictions (techniques and validation); adaptivity on new forecast problems, rapid prototyping techniques for forecasting; generalization capabilities of demonstrators, integration in existing EMS; and effectiveness of intelligent tools for the real world.

articleTitle: An evolution strategy for common unit commitment and economic dispatch of hydrothermal power systems
abstract: This paper reports on a new approach to solve the short-term operation-planning problem of hydrothermal power systems. It uses evolution strategies to achieve a solution of the complex mixed-integer nonlinear optimization problem without any decomposition of the original planning problem. Some extensions of conventional evolution strategies were necessary to include inequality constraints and integer variables. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the proposed method is able to find a solution in an acceptable computation time.

articleTitle: Influence of load behavior on service restoration
abstract: An extended fault in a distribution system may pose problems during feeder restoration. Immediately after energizing the feeder, high currents may arise due to a phenomenon called cold load pick-up (CLPU), causing activation of the overcurrent protection and preventing immediate reconnection of all load. The feeder should be sectioned and the restoration performed in steps. In the paper, an algorithm for determination of a sequence of restoration actions is presented. The algorithm determines the maximum number of customers that can be reconnected immediately and recommends time delays to restore the remaining sections with regards to the setting of overcurrent protection. The results of a restoration simulation on a part of the Slovenian distribution system are presented in the paper.

articleTitle: A diakoptical technique for harmonic power flow of large scale 3-phase power systems
abstract: This paper represents a new harmonic power flow algorithm for a large-scale distribution system. The phase coordinates method is used to model the distribution system as a frequency dependent network. The bus admittance matrix is obtained as a sparse matrix in the block diagonal band form using a piece-wise method. An appropriate algorithm is given for more than one harmonic source condition and for loop, radial or mixed systems.

articleTitle: Modern technology in control center operation
abstract: The development of computer technology enabled significant improvements in dispatching centers. That was especially important for Croatian Electricity that was faced with a prospect of a new way of operation with new functions and responsibilities. The financial situation did not allow complete replacement of the computer system and its software support. This paper describes the interconnection of the new hardware with the existing hardware, improvements and new technologies introduced to control center operation and the development of a new control system.

articleTitle: Some problems of the partial opening of the electricity market
abstract: The opening of the electricity market requires changes in the structure and operation of the power system. This paper deals with the possible minimization of the costs occurring at the partial opening of the market and the relationship of the electricity cost and availability of supply for customers connected to different network sources.

articleTitle: Accuracy assessment of hydro power plants models
abstract: In the paper, the issue of cascade hydro system scheduling is addressed. Various techniques for hydro power plants modeling are discussed and a detailed comparison of various models is given. First, a detailed simulation model of a generic hydro power plant is presented. Although computationally very demanding, it produces perfectly accurate results. Therefore it can be used as a reference. To describe the operation of a hydro power plant, relation between the power generation and water discharge has to be known. The traditional approach to finding this relation is to utilize a polynomial function. To obtain better performance, new models based on neural networks are developed. The developed models are tested for a cascade hydro system on the Soca river and some results are reported.

articleTitle: Novel technique to predict dry-band arcing failure of fiber-optic cables installed on high voltage lines
abstract: Utilities frequently use ADSS (all dielectric self-supporting) fiber-optic cables installed on transmission lines. Dry-band arcing occurs on the fiber-optic cables when they are polluted and wet. The objective of this paper is to present a technique to predict dry-band arcing in fiber-optic cables. An equivalent circuit is used to represent the polluted fiber-optic cable. The effect of pollution levels on voltage and current distribution along the fiber-optic cable is analyzed. The longitudinal field and power loss distribution along the fiber-optic cable is analyzed. It is shown that for heavy pollution levels, the space potential can be exceeded. The effect of span length on voltage and current is analyzed. The effect of sag on the space potential is analyzed. This model can be used by utilities to predict dry-band arcing in fiber-optic cables installed on transmission lines.

articleTitle: The harmonic contents of electronic device currents: experimental, qualitative and theoretical analysis
abstract: This paper examines the harmonic contents of input currents (ICs) of electronic devices (EDs), such as computers, power supplies, various measurement devices, etc. All types of EDs have similar nonsinusoidal wave form of the ICs. An explanation of the peculiarities of the device ICs is presented. Several criteria, which allow clustering the EDs in three groups are defined. For each group the distortion effects, caused by different EDs, are estimated.

articleTitle: The levelized reserve capacity method for the maintenance scheduling of the generating units
abstract: In this paper, the computational procedures for generating unit maintenance scheduling using the levelized reserve capacity method are given by using an example system. The rates obtained are used to estimate the power plant's capacity factors. The influence of the generating unit's maintenance is taken into account in the obtained energy output of each generating unit, production cost and the power system's reliability.

articleTitle: Investigation of nodal prices in a deregulated competitive market-case studies
abstract: Deregulation is causing a great impact on the electric power industry around the world. Many transactions in electric power markets are based on bidding competition after deregulation. The nodal price plays an important role in such a kind of market to reflect the bidding strategy for a market participant. This paper investigates the impact of ancillary service, security constraint, and MW loss on nodal prices in the system. The causes for the variation of nodal prices are explained. The problem is formulated with DC models and solved by simplex linear programming. The simulation results help understand the meaning of the nodal prices and help develop bidding strategies for the market participants.

articleTitle: Commercialization risks in the Brazilian market
abstract: This paper describes the main characteristics of the Brazilian electrical sector and the main features of the its restructuring process. It is highlighted that the trading arrangements will be based around a tight pool scheme, i.e., a central optimization system dispatch procedure in which the spot price will be based on the short run marginal cost. As the Brazilian system is hydro dominated, these spot prices present an intrinsic volatility due to the uncertainties associated to future inflows to the reservoirs. In this way, the hydrological risk provokes commercialization risks for which possible mitigation mechanisms are discussed. Finally, a case study considering the risk aspects of inserting a new thermal power plant in the Brazilian hydrothermal system is discussed as well as the impact of a long term contract to reduce the exposure to the spot prices.

articleTitle: Virtual Design Studio: new approach to computer aided design of power electromagnetic devices
abstract: Approaches to developing a virtual environment for design and study of complex electromagnetic systems are presented. Development results of decision making methods, mathematical simulation of electric machines and devices, and numerical methods of nonlinear electromagnetic field problem solving are reflected in this paper.

articleTitle: The role of the power companies in the fuel cell market
abstract: The European power companies are concentrating their efforts primarily at increasing the competitive edge of their companies by means of cost optimization programs, leaving very little free space for new power generation techniques. Fuel cells are a new and promising technology. This article illustrates that there are good opportunities for fuel cells to gain a foothold in the market, even under the pressure of competitive conditions. The retail market in particular offers excellent preconditions for this undertaking. Success decisively depends on the development of cost-optimized systems which can be installed in the user's plant at a low expenditure.

articleTitle: Transmission charging for the Greek Electric Power System
abstract: This paper deals with the costing of transmission services and compares different methodologies for transmission charges allocation among the players involved in the Greek Power System. The main issues analyzed in this paper are use of system charge and cost of transmission system losses.

articleTitle: A reduced order model to solving the economic dispatch problem
abstract: This paper presents a new method for solving the economic dispatch problem. Loads are first modeled by appropriate voltage dependent models as admittances and then added to the bus admittance matrix and their respective buses are eliminated. The variables of the obtained reduced model are the voltage-controlled buses' angles and active power generations. The variables are calculated by the Newton Raphson method while minimizing operational cost. Load bus voltages of the original system are then calculated by a direct method and load admittances are modified. The process is repeated until convergence is achieved.

articleTitle: Voltage stability studies in multimachine power systems
abstract: In this paper the dynamic voltage stability of multimachine power system is discussed. A new power-flow method, which has no convergence problem near the point of loadability limit is developed and used to trace P-V curves. From the P-V curves the weakest bus of the system is identified and then the multimachine power system is reduced to an equivalent single-machine-load-bus (SMLB) system. Using the equivalent system a method of designing the reactive power compensation and the critical time before which the compensation has to be applied is presented.

articleTitle: Power system stabilization based on power swing linearization controlled by UPFC
abstract: The authors have developed a practical scheme for the direct power control of a generator to linearize the power swing characteristics, which brings a robust power system stabilizing control. This paper describes the effectiveness and robustness of proposed control experimentally confirmed in a 10 kVA model power transmission system with a UPFC.

articleTitle: Online dynamic security control in a large scale power system
abstract: Summary form only given. The aim of this paper is to introduce a new methodology, based on dynamic optimization, for assessing preventive control actions to guarantee dynamic security of power systems. In order to mitigate the effect of a contingency, in terms of steady-state or transient violation such as overloads, unacceptable transient voltage dips, system instability, preventive actions are applied as soon as a potentially dangerous violation is detected during a contingency screening. The proposed approach entails the ability to force the system trajectories in an acceptable state space domain under a set of severe but credible contingencies and gives indications about preventive actions when necessary. The approach is sufficiently general to improve the transient behavior of a power system with regard to different objectives such as: to enforce angle stability of the system constraining rotor angle deviations and minimizing the integral of transient kinetic energy across the whole trajectory; and to avoid transient voltage stability using a signal energy based on an integral form of the voltage magnitude at each bus of the system. This methodology consists of an optimization procedure where: the objective function is aimed at minimizing control action efforts; inequality constraints confine the trajectory of the system in a practical domain of the state space ensuring a feasible behavior of the system, power quality, etc.; and equality constraints derive from the discretization of the differential-algebraic equations of the power system sparse representation.

articleTitle: Effect of power frequency magnetic field on image of computer monitor
abstract: In order to systematically investigate the effect of a power frequency magnetic field on an image of a computer monitor, a Merritt-type coil was constructed which is enable to produce uniform field space inside the coil. The magnetic field which causes the inception of flicker was experimentally obtained. Furthermore, examination was made on the reduction in magnetic field inside a shielding box which was developed for the minimization of such a flicker problem. The quantification of environmental magnetic field inside houses is also evaluated.

articleTitle: A three phase load flow program for industrial power system analysis
abstract: This paper describes a three-phase load flow method for the steady state analysis of an industrial power system under all possible unbalance conditions. The load flow problem formulation and solution are done in the phase frame reference. Detailed models for generators, transmission lines and cables, transformers and bus loads are utilized.

articleTitle: Leakage current measuring methodology for surge arresters in field testing
abstract: The paper presents a new method for the measurement of the leakage current of surge arresters. A prototype version of the current transducer is developed and a series of experimental studies on a large number of arresters are carried out. Thus obtained measurements were examined in detail. The main objective of this research is to improve the measurement equipment and diagnostic methods for the field testing of metal-oxide surge arresters as well as conventional arresters.

articleTitle: The determination of supply harmonic currents produced by multiple PWM voltage source inverter induction motor drives: an expert system approach
abstract: An expert system approach is described for the determination of 3-phase AC supply line 5/sup th/ and 7/sup th/ harmonic currents produced by multiple PWM inverter induction motor drives connected in parallel to the supply system and operating at their rated power outputs. The approach is illustrated using the simulated performance. The master rule structure of the expert system is described and further development of the knowledge base is briefly discussed.

articleTitle: Measurement of lightning strike current effects on an airplane fuselage test setup
abstract: During the investigation, an aluminum test cylinder, representative in size and construction of a fighter-type aircraft fuselage, was subjected to high current pulses, similar to lightning return strokes. The objective of this full scale test technique was to assess the susceptibility of aircraft electrical circuits to lightning. Tests were conducted to determine the magnitude of magnetic flux density inside the cylinder as a result of lightning current flowing on the cylinder surface. The initial phase of the investigation was the modeling of the entire experimental circuit in order to calculate the total surface current and compare it to the measured values. During the second phase, a new technique was developed for the measurement of the magnetic field distribution outside and inside along the test cylinder during the simulated lightning surges. An example is given: the measured ratio of the voltage outputs of two magnetic flux density probes at two test points, one outside and one inside the closed aluminum test cylinder, was about 4700.

articleTitle: Using self-organizing map in identification of load-loss state
abstract: This paper presents a self-organizing map (SOM) based method for power system load-loss state classification. This classifier maps vectors of an N-dimensional space to a 2-dimensional net in a nonlinear way while preserving the topological order of the input vectors. Input features to SOM are real and reactive power at each load bus and available real power generation at each generation bus. After the training of the SOM, the generalization capability of the SOM can cope with various operating conditions which have not been encountered during the training phase and hence give a correct classification result. The effectiveness of the proposed method has been demonstrated on a 9-bus test system. This proposed method is useful for power system operation, power system reliability assessment and state screening.

articleTitle: The using of computers to demonstrate the visual impacts of the industrial objects in environment
abstract: Because of the increasing environmental problems and the limited industrial areas, day by day it is more difficult to have industrial objects accepted by public opinion. This is especially true for the right-of-way of industrial objects e.g. for new transmission lines and substations. In Hungarian practice, investors and designers use different computer methods to help demonstrate the visual impacts of these objects to the public opinion and land owners.

articleTitle: Rotation speed controller for AC motor drives with frequency converters
abstract: The paper presents a controller for AC motor drives with frequency converters. It controls output frequency of the converter and in such a way-rotation speed of the motor according to the sensor signals to keep the given value of some parameter of the system, e.g. water pressure in water pump outlet, constant. The suggested controller is based on comparators and an operation amplifier. It can be used for rotation speed control of pumps and fans in heating, ventilating and air conditioning or in flow applications. The controller is simple, cheap and is user friendly.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic transient phenomena in HVDC converter station
abstract: In the paper the results of transient electromagnetic phenomena simulations at switching and fault conditions in an AC/DC power system are presented. The mathematical simulations of transient phenomena were realised with the use of the ATP/EMTP program. For the ATP program, the method for thyristor valves control, utilising subprogram models, are prepared. In conclusion, the essential results of simulations of transient electromagnetic phenomena in converter stations of AC/DC power systems are presented. The results of simulations may be used for the selection of overvoltage and overcurrent protection devices and for recommended sequences of switching operations.

articleTitle: Intelligent application at the 400/120 kV substation of the Pars nuclear power plant
abstract: A complete reconstruction program was started at the electrical substation of the Paks nuclear power plant to assist the Hungarian high voltage network to join the European network. At the operator level a new, PC-based SCADA system was introduced. An AI-based, intelligent advisory system was developed and embedded into the SCADA system. The first part of the paper shows the substation and the hardware-software environment of the intelligent system, The second part describes the advisory functions and their realizations in rules and procedures, Besides increasing reliability and safety of energy supply, the basic goal of the system is to assist the operator in faster and more effective reactions if something irregular happens at the substation, and to assist the plant engineer to better understand and evaluate what was happening.

articleTitle: Monitoring of synchronous generators transients on manifolds of equilibria
abstract: In this paper a detailed model of a synchronous machine with a special orthogonal structure is discussed. The model is expanded by the effect of magnetic saturation with respect to analytical frame given by the unsaturated orthogonal model. The necessity of including cross-magnetization effects is reviewed. From the complete model of a saturated synchronous machine, which has also an orthogonal structure, analytical expressions can be derived easily to make a statement about all possible equilibrium points. The effect of magnetic saturation on the equilibrium points with respect to particular parameters is discussed with an extended model. For small currents this extended model with saturation converges steadily towards the model without saturation. The theory of the behavior of dynamical systems "near" manifolds of equilibria is used for monitoring of internal states of synchronous generators.

articleTitle: Advanced measuring system for the complex analysis of dielectric parameters and PD-phenomena
abstract: This paper reports on the integration of PD measurements to a compact and computer-based insulation test system which allows, for the first time, the simultaneous measurement of both the impedance parameters of HV insulation and the partial discharge behavior. Additionally, PD faults can be located. For analyzing characteristic PD types, a fault databank based expert system is integrated. With it, the complete insulation condition can be assessed in a complex manner. The system is characterized by a general modular conception. It is designed to implement most of the functionality in digital-components, exclusively. The implementation of different acquisition units is cascadable. In this paper, a brief survey is presented on the different measuring procedures integrated in the device.

articleTitle: Breakdown characteristics of CO/sub 2/ and N/sub 2/ containing SF/sub 6/
abstract: AC breakdown strengths of CO/sub 2/, N/sub 2/, SF/sub 6/ and the mixtures of CO/sub 2/+SF/sub 6/ and N/sub 2/+SF/sub 6/ containing 0.5% and 4% of SF/sub 6/ in nonuniform field were experimentally studied. The relative gas pressure was varied within the range of 100-500 kPa and the electrode gap spacing was 25 mm. The experimental results have shown that the addition of SF/sub 6/ to CO/sub 2/ and N/sub 2/ causes a significant increase the AC breakdown voltage with respect to CO/sub 2/ and N/sub 2/ within the range of defined pressures.

articleTitle: Electrical distribution system reconfiguration for future meshed networks
abstract: This paper presents a heuristic reconfiguration algorithm developed for implementation in a very flexible meshed network with remote controlled switches for real-time operating mode. The purpose is that of on-line minimisation of network operation costs over a time period, mainly through minimisation of power losses and the number of switching operations, preserving at the same time load balancing. The algorithm's ability to perform an efficient optimal reconfiguration in normal operating condition has been tested in reference to a different degree of complexity of the meshed network which it is applied to.

articleTitle: A new scattering matrix-based formulation for electric power systems
abstract: This paper offers three contributions. First, it introduces a novel scattering approach to the load flow problem resulting in a geometric representation of its solutions. Second, it introduces a decentralized load flow approach by which information about another load can be determined from local measurements at a different bus. Third, it introduces scattering matrix based measures of power network capacity, again using a geometric approach. The concepts proposed are illustrated on a three bus power network.

articleTitle: Improved method for flicker evaluation
abstract: The paper deals with the sensitivity of the flicker measurement according to IEC 868 and EN 50160 requirements on the start time at the measurement. Furthermore evaluation methods are introduced to improve the stability of the long term flicker sensitivity factor relative to the start time of the measurement.

articleTitle: Using current-magnitude measurements in decoupled state estimation
abstract: In this paper, a new fast-decoupled algorithm is presented to handle the current magnitude (CM) measurements. This method is based on the equivalent-current-measurements (ECM) in rectangular coordinates. Both the power and CM measurement are converted into the ECM form. The method produces a constant symmetric gain matrix, which can be decoupled into two identical sub-gain matrices. It is very efficient because one sub-gain matrix is used and needs to be factorized only once. The weighted least square (WLS) approach is employed to solve this problem. Tests have shown that the proposed method could outperform other formulations and have a great potential for online operations.

articleTitle: The determination of the stability regions via the controlling unstable equilibrium points in AC-DC system transient stability analysis
abstract: In this paper, a sequential integrated AC-DC system transient stability analysis is accomplished by taking into account the variation of the amplitude of the bus voltages during transient. This variation of the bus voltages is provided by power-flow analysis of the AC-DC system with respect to the modified active power, since the active power transferred through the DC line changes at each integration step. Thus, the AC-DC transient stability analysis is accomplished considering the true value of the ratio of the reactive power absorbed from the converters to the active power transferred through DC line by the sequential approach. In this study, the DC line is taken into consideration as a monopolar one and is also represented as the current injections to the buses where it is connected and its effect is reflected at the internal buses in the form of additional bus power injections. The system loads are also represented as current injections to the buses where they are connected. The effect of these is again reflected at the internal buses in the form of additional bus power injections. Thus, the problem in not constructing a valid Lyapunov function due to the transfer conductance is eliminated.

articleTitle: Talking into account power system reaction in problems of multicriteria optimizing network configuration in distribution systems
abstract: Two lines of improving the validity and efficiency in solving problems of network reconfiguration in distribution systems are considered. One line is associated with taking into account a power system reaction while minimizing power or energy losses. Different techniques for constructing power system functional equivalents are considered and illustrated. Another line is related to formulating the problems within the framework of a multicriteria optimization model to consider and to minimize diverse indices. Analysis of the model is based on the Bellman-Zadeh approach to decision making in a fuzzy environment.

articleTitle: Adaptive equivalenting for calculations of electric power system state
abstract: Two algorithms of correction of balanced steady states of electric power systems at local disturbances are suggested. The basis of the suggested approach is the method of automatic construction of a network equivalent, adequate to the place and size of the disturbing effect. The proposed approach allows one to sharply reduce the volume of calculations and requirements to the computer resources. The sphere of application is correction of state, calculations of the higher harmonics under nonsinusoidal states, correction of the state estimations, other tasks.

articleTitle: Three-phase fast decoupled power flow
abstract: This paper presents power flow methods for the solution of unbalanced and balanced three-phase distribution systems. The best existing methods for solving three-phase power flow are tested and the results discussed. The fast decoupled methods and the current injection Newton work for radial and meshed networks, and the matrices (Jacobian) remain constant, but the backward/forward sweep is appropriated for radial systems and works for a weakly meshed network. For general systems, the BX methods have presented the best performance.

articleTitle: Reliability analyses and design on excitation controller of synchronous generator
abstract: In this paper, the fault tree analysis method is used to analyze the reliability of excitation controller of synchronous generator. The structural block of the controller is constructed based on its operation principle. Then the controller's fault tree can be automatically drawn out based on the failure mode of every unit or component. The reliable degree of controller can be calculated and the curve of its reliable degree function can be drawn out according to the chosen failure rate of every component and unit.

articleTitle: Separation of nonlinear combined reactive load
abstract: The paper deals with a novel approach of simulation of nonlinear voltage dependent load characteristics especially applicable in load flow and in electrodynamic stability modeling. The novel method introduces the voltage dependent exponent to characterize nonlinear loads. Furthermore, a method is introduced enabling the separation of a mixed (inductive and capacitive) nonlinear load onto an inductive and capacitive component.

articleTitle: A decentralised fuzzy stabiliser for multimachine power system
abstract: The paper proposes a new power system stabilizer able to enhance multimachine power system stability. To achieve this aim a suitable model has been determined by feedback linearization and a new fuzzy controller is proposed. In the paper, the numerical results on a classical four nodes power system are reported.

articleTitle: The impact of flywheel torque of refurbished generator units on the limit switching time in Croatian power system
abstract: In a refurbishment project, possible solutions for old generators in Zakucac and Peruca hydroelectric power plants (HPP), Croatia, are suggested. In the first step, transient processes caused by 3-phase and phase-earth short circuits on all connected transmission lines to Zakucac and Peruca HPPs were analysed on the different power system models. Many computer calculations of transient stability in Zakucac and Peruca HPP and dependent environment of the power system with refurbished generators in these plants were made. Since transient stability in the power system with recommended characteristics of refurbished generator units were satisfied, the impacts of smaller flywheel torque on limit switching time values were considered in a second step.

articleTitle: EMC-measures for underground power cables
abstract: Shielding-measures against the magnetic field of underground cables can lead to reductions of the current rating. This problem can be eliminated by laying the cables in a pipe, which is cooled by free or forced convection of the ambient air. This system allows heat recovery of the cable losses and thereby an essential improvement of the efficiency of the power transmission, combined with a low or even disappearing outer magnetic field.

articleTitle: Permissible current rating of the investigated 110 kV underground cable line
abstract: This paper analysis the influence of the soil kind and its drying out on the permissible current rating of a 110 kV underground cable line, located in Belgrade area. The analysis is carried out by means of modified mathematical model of IEC Publication 287 and the results of long term test investigations of the local soil thermal behavior along the cable route. The soil around the cables is treated with simplified physical model. It is supposed that the local soil along the cable route consists from two layers with different kinds and diameters of the dried out soil zone around 110 kV single-core cables in trefoil formation.

articleTitle: Simulation of power systems by wave digital filter principles, a case study: interconnected multimachine systems
abstract: The digital signal processing methodology known as wave digital filters (WD) transforms analog networks into topological equivalent digital filters. Such a feature makes WD a powerful technique for simulating power system transients. Every WD filter can be considered to be a digital model of a certain continuous-time filter or a network, called its reference filter or reference network. In many respects, both the reference filter and the WD filter behave similarly. For example, if the reference filter is passive or lossless, the corresponding WD filter will be passive or lossless, respectively. Although the concept of WD filtering was originally introduced to simulate linear circuits, it can be applied to nonlinear networks as well.

articleTitle: A microcontroller based control of current source converter fed reversing induction motor drive
abstract: In this paper a microcontroller based control of CSI fed induction motor drive is proposed. The goal of this work is to design the reversing induction motor drive with appropriate vector control implemented in only one microcontroller to reduce the cost of the drive. To obtain the same performances that exist in other vector controlled drives, a several improvements in control algorithm were made. All results that are accomplished in a various experiments confirm the exactness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Power factor correction for intermittent and fluctuating loads
abstract: This paper reports case studies of capacitors for marble plant application, as an example of time varying loads. The marble process depends largely upon the thickness and polished surface of the marble block. During the cutting and polishing processes, these conditions cause strictly time-varying active and reactive power and also produce unbalanced varying load at low varying power factors. This paper presents the measurement results of an electrical parameter survey of marble loads. It also discusses the selection of capacitor banks according to harmonic currents.

articleTitle: Microprocessor-based out-of-phase reclosing protection for nonutility generation units
abstract: Protection against an out of phase reconnection with the utility power network is one of the most important protection requirements for nonutility generation (NUG) units, since an out-of-phase reclosing will certainly damage the rotating equipment and windings of a generator. Power system test studies presented show that the power-based protection algorithm provides a very good performance for reliable detection of out-of-phase reclosing conditions.

articleTitle: Investigation of the effect of control scheme for the SMES with solid-state phase shifter (SuperSMES) on power system stabilization
abstract: The SuperSMES, which is a combination of superconducting magnetic energy storage (SMES) and solid-state phase shifter, is expected to become a new effective apparatus in power systems. This paper shows the results of a new stabilizing control scheme of the SuperSMES for power system stabilization based on experimental results with a 10 kJ superconducting magnet and a 10 kVA model power transmission line. In this paper, the relation between control mode of the SuperSMES for power system stabilization and subsynchronous resonance (SSR) has been also investigated.

articleTitle: Design and manufacturing of cable penetrations for the Paks Nuclear Power Plant, Hungary
abstract: The paper deals with the design and manufacture of cable penetrations developed and manufactured in Hungary for application in reactor buildings of WWER 440 type nuclear power plants. The basic requirements and the working principle of the low voltage penetrations are described. Special attention is devoted to the hermetic and /spl gamma/-shielding system having a primary importance in protection of the environment in the event of an accident. Type tests and long term service experiences proving the reliability of penetrations are referred to. Some parameters of available products are also listed.

articleTitle: Measurement and analysis of electric power quality in power system networks
abstract: In the report some results of research of electric power quality (EPQ) in power system networks of Ukraine are considered. The approach to realization of measurements of electric power quality indices (EPQI) values as random variables, and evaluation of results of measurement are considered. Because of the analysis of a state of EPQ in power networks of some power system substations, a number of practical conclusions are made. They are expedient for use in realization of measurement with the purpose of work reduction and increase of measurement efficiencies.

articleTitle: Static compensation systems for improving electric power quality
abstract: Summary form only given. The supply of electrical energy to loads in industrial plants has some undesirable repercussions on the supply network. Depending upon the type of load and its mode of operation, the reactions are usually a reduction in the power factor, system voltage fluctuations, voltage flicker, unbalanced loading of the three phases and harmonic currents, which in turn affect negatively the electric power quality. The subject of this paper is to study and analyze the main reasons for such undesirable reactions and to find the compensation system required for each reaction to reduce its effect to an acceptable level, such as either switched capacitor banks or high response thyristor controlled reactors. To improve the electric power quality, these systems may be augmented by adding filters for eliminating discrete harmonics or harmonic bands.

articleTitle: Profitable power exchanges and available transmission capacity between two large systems: the example of the European TESIS-UPS Interconnection
abstract: The TESIS-UPS interconnection Project aimed at assessing the requirements and the feasibility of synchronous interconnection between the Trans European Synchronously Interconnected System (TESIS) system and the Unified Power System (UPS). It is financed by the European Community (TACIS fund). As a first stage of this study, the combination of an economical analysis together with a network study allow to assess clearly the level of exchanges together with the network consistency to be considered.

articleTitle: Rigidity concept for stabilizing transient processes in power systems
abstract: This paper introduces a totally new concept of rigidity and its first example applications for stabilizing transient processes in power systems. By the authors' definition, a rigid system maintains a close-to-original state despite passing disturbances or smoothly goes over to a new state if the disturbances are permanent; it responds to faults and disturbances with a smooth monotonous or minimum oscillatory behavior. Rigidity implies stability. A rigid system is stable because it applies all state variables to be at least bounded. In contrast to stability, rigidity has a quite simple and convenient mathematical description. It provides an objective function that can be optimized along the transient trajectory to obtain effective stabilizing control impacts. Several different online control actions can be selected in coordination for a variety of operating conditions, controlled variables and uncertainties. The rigidity criterion can be easily computed by using the output files of any transient simulation program.

articleTitle: Performance characteristics of an OPF for allocation of VArs in a competitive environment
abstract: This paper presents a linear programming (LP) based direct reactive optimal power flow (OFF) to optimally allocate reactive power in a given instantaneous state of a system. The main focus of the paper is on accuracy and convergence rate of the developed OFF. The issue of performance characteristics arises from the inability of the LP based OPF to converge spontaneously. A bound reduction heuristics technique is developed to enforce the convergence of the OPF. Extensive case studies are carried out on the IEEE-118 bus system to illustrate the impact of different bound reduction parameters on the convergence rate and the accuracy of the solution.

articleTitle: A system approach to emergency load shedding in case of voltage instability
abstract: In this paper, the load shedding algorithm based on system approach to prevent voltage instability is presented. The main point of the algorithm is the on-line linear optimization model, which produces the amounts of the load that need to be shed in the case of emergency voltage condition. Thus, the load shedding is simultaneously performed at all regional buses which enables voltage recovery at the jeopardized critical bus. Within the proposed optimization model, special attention is paid to the directly controlled loads since their disconnection does not significantly disturb the operating policy. The proposed procedure is verified on the example of the real high-voltage power system.

articleTitle: A minimal cost design for a harmonic reduction system: a petrochemical plant example
abstract: In this paper, the design of a harmonic reduction system based on passive filter is proposed for a case study based on a realistic arrangement of a petrochemical plant. The test system is characterized by 55 buses, 7 generators, nonlinear loads and electrical drives. The four electrical drives considered in the system are characterized by a rated power ranging from 4 to 15 MW. The aim of the paper is to design a harmonic reduction system able to satisfy the standard IEEE 519-1992 and guarantee a minimal cost solution.

articleTitle: A power system Java-based distributed database design
abstract: The great bulk of data that characterises the EMS/DMS supervisor monitoring or control actions comports noteworthy system information management problems. It is important to adopt a new modelling philosophy that allows in a simple but efficient manner the system state representation within an open architecture environment. In this paper, the power system is represented through a distributed database, using the big object modelling (BOM) technique to model each of its components, that allows a quick and wide access to all system information.

articleTitle: Problems of power system frequency and active power control
abstract: This paper illustrates the result of research done by authors in the area of frequency and active power control. For interconnected power systems, besides common frequency regulation, there is a need to control tie-line load flows. Control problems can be divided into two parts: control of normal and emergency conditions. The reasons for an interconnection's oscillations are considered as is a new method for regulation of frequency without oscillations.
